title: The Birdland package tour with Basie, Joe Williams and Sarah Vaughan
summary: Jones conducted the Basie band for Sarah on a mid-1950s package with Eckstine, Hibbler and Getz, where Joe Williams and Basie were hard to follow.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Were you associated with Duke's band during the time that Hibbler was with it, or was that later?
No, Hibbler, he was a single act at that point.
Uh-huh.
And he was booked with -- this was with the Basie Band. And I was with -- oh, we had Joe Williams,

Sarah, had four singers on there, very good singers on there. Had Al Hibbler, Billy Eckstine and Sarah. And Stan Getz, Zoot Sims. It was a very good package, you know? A very sharp package. (Unintelligible) Phineas Newborn.
You were with the Basie band.
Well, I was accompanying Sarah.
Oh, uh-huh.
Sarah Vaughan, you know. And she was using my scores and whatever scores she had. So I had to conduct the band.
I see.
And this was the band that -- they had Thad Jones, and they had really -- Frank Foster, Frank Wes$, Ernie Wilkins. That was a heavyweight band, I call it.
This was what year?
Middle '50s, I guess. This is When the (Unintelligible) 'Okay, You Win... ' 'All Right, Okay, You Win.'
(Unintelligible).
Yeah. And what's the other one? 'Every Day.'
Uh-huh.
These were the big hits. And then Joe Williams and Count Basie had the strong team.
Uh-huh.
You know? And it was very hard to follow

them, so Billy Eckstine, before he signed his contract, he said, "You'd better put Joe Williams up front," because none of them could follow him at that point, because he and Count Basie had such a strong team. Sarah Vaughan and Al Hibbler and everybody just got out of the way. Said well, we'll take an intermission. You know, just let the show go, take an intermission, so they can forget about Joe Williams.
(Laughter)
